title: UNIT 3: MATRICES
notes:
✓ Matrix → a rectangular arrangement of numbers in rows and columns.

◆ Row → horizontal arrangement.
◆ Column → vertical arrangement.
◆ Entry/element → a number inside a matrix.
◆ Order → number of rows × number of columns.

Example:
A = [ 2  4  6 ]
       [ 1  3  5 ]

A is a 2 × 3 matrix.
It has 2 rows, 3 columns and 6 entries.

title: 3.1  CONCEPTS AND TYPES OF MATRICES
notes:
A matrix is written as A = [aᵢⱼ], where aᵢⱼ is the entry in row i and column j.

◆ Row matrix → one row.
◆ Column matrix → one column.
◆ Square matrix → same number of rows and columns.
◆ Rectangular matrix → different numbers of rows and columns.

Example:
A = [ 1  2  3 ]  → row matrix

B = [ 1 ]        → column matrix
       [ 2 ]

C = [ 1  2 ]     → square matrix
       [ 3  4 ]

title: SPECIAL MATRICES
notes:
◆ Zero matrix → all entries are 0.

◆ Identity matrix → square matrix with 1s on the main diagonal and 0s elsewhere.

I₂ = [ 1  0 ]
     [ 0  1 ]

◆ Diagonal matrix → all entries outside the main diagonal are 0.

[ 3  0  0 ]
[ 0  5  0 ]
[ 0  0  7 ]

◆ Scalar matrix → diagonal matrix with equal diagonal entries.

[ 4  0 ]
[ 0  4 ]

title: SYMMETRIC AND TRIANGULAR MATRICES
notes:
✓ Symmetric matrix → Aᵀ = A.

Example:
A = [ 2  3 ]
       [ 3  5 ]

◆ Upper triangular matrix → all entries below the main diagonal are 0.

[ 2  4  5 ]
[ 0  3  6 ]
[ 0  0  7 ]

◆ Lower triangular matrix → all entries above the main diagonal are 0.

[ 2  0  0 ]
[ 4  3  0 ]
[ 5  6  7 ]

title: 3.2 OPERATIONS ON MATRICES
notes:
✓ Matrix addition and subtraction → corresponding entries are added or subtracted.

→ Matrices must have the same order.

Example:
A = [ 1  2 ]    B = [ 5  6 ]
       [ 3  4 ]           [ 7  8 ]

A + B = [ 6   8 ]
            [10  12 ]

A − B = [ −4  −4 ]
            [ −4  −4 ]

✓ Scalar multiplication → multiply every entry by the scalar.

2A = [ 2  4 ]
        [ 6  8 ]

title: MATRIX MULTIPLICATION
notes:
✓ Matrix multiplication is possible when:

→ Columns of the first matrix = rows of the second matrix.

If A is m × p and B is p × n:
AB is m × n.

Example:
A = [ 1  2 ]    B = [ 5  6 ]
       [ 3  4 ]            [ 7  8 ]

AB = [19  22]
         [43  50]

→ Each entry is found by multiplying a row of A by a column of B.

Generally:
AB ≠ BA.

title: TRANSPOSE OF A MATRIX
notes:
✓ Transpose → interchange rows and columns.

The transpose of A is written Aᵀ.

Example:
A = [ 1  2  3 ]
        [ 4  5  6 ]

Aᵀ = [ 1  4 ]
         [ 2  5 ]
        [ 3  6 ]

If A is m × n, then Aᵀ is n × m.

Important properties:
(Aᵀ)ᵀ = A

(A + B)ᵀ = Aᵀ + Bᵀ

(AB)ᵀ = BᵀAᵀ.

title: 3.3 ELEMENTARY ROW OPERATIONS
notes:
✓ Elementary row operations are used to transform matrices and solve systems of equations.

1. Row interchange:
R₁ ↔ R₂

2. Row multiplication:
R₁ → kR₁, k ≠ 0

3. Row replacement:
R₂ → R₂ + kR₁

Example:
[ 1  2 ]
[ 3  4 ]

R₂ → R₂ − 3R₁

[ 1   2 ]
[ 0  −2 ]

→ These operations are the basis of Gaussian elimination.

title: SYSTEMS OF LINEAR EQUATIONS
notes:
✓ A system of linear equations contains two or more linear equations involving the same variables.

Example:
x + y = 5
x − y = 1

It can be written in matrix form as:

AX = B

A = [ 1   1 ]
       [ 1  −1 ]

X = [ x ]
       [ y ]

B = [ 5 ]
       [ 1 ]

→ The system can be solved using an augmented matrix and row operations.

title: GAUSSIAN ELIMINATION & SOLUTIONS
notes:
✓ Gaussian elimination → use elementary row operations to reduce an augmented matrix to Row Echelon Form (REF), then solve by back-substitution.

◆ One solution → unique solution.
◆ No solution → contradiction such as 0 = 5.
◆ Infinitely many solutions → at least one free variable and no contradiction.

Example:
[ 1  1 | 5 ]
[ 1 −1 | 1 ]

R₂ → R₂ − R₁:

[ 1   1 | 5 ]
[ 0  −2 | −4 ]

Therefore:
y = 2 and x = 3.

Solution = (3, 2).

title: INVERSE OF A MATRIX
notes:
✓ Inverse of A → a matrix A⁻¹ satisfying:

AA⁻¹ = A⁻¹A = I.

◆ A matrix with an inverse is called non-singular/invertible.
◆ A matrix without an inverse is singular.

To find an inverse using row operations:

[A | I] → [I | A⁻¹]

Example:
A = [ 1  2 ]
    [ 3  7 ]

Start with:
[ 1  2 | 1  0 ]
[ 3  7 | 0  1 ]

→ Reduce the left side to I. The right side becomes A⁻¹.

title: UNIT 3 KEY FORMULAS & QUICK REVISION
notes:
◆ Order → rows × columns.

◆ Matrix addition/subtraction → same order required.

◆ Matrix multiplication → columns of A = rows of B.

◆ If A is m × p and B is p × n → AB is m × n.

◆ Identity → AI = IA = A.

◆ Transpose → rows ↔ columns.

◆ Symmetric → Aᵀ = A.

◆ Row operations → interchange, multiplication, replacement.

◆ Linear system → AX = B.

◆ Augmented matrix → [A | B].

◆ Gaussian elimination → REF + back-substitution.

◆ Inverse → AA⁻¹ = A⁻¹A = I.

◆ Inverse by row operations → [A | I] → [I | A⁻¹].

✓ Remember: Matrix multiplication is generally NOT commutative: AB ≠ BA.
